title: An unchanged cardiac-arrest prediction model retained discrimination in a confirmatory and external retrospective evaluation
summary: An existing ICU cardiac-arrest model was evaluated in a retrospective confirmatory sample and an independent external hospital cohort. It retained discrimination and detected more pre-arrest prediction points than conventional scores at matched alarm burden. The study tests retrospective performance, not intervention benefit.
ai_technology: An existing recurrent-network and gradient-boosting ensemble estimates 12-hour cardiac-arrest risk from ICU data.
organization: VUNO Inc., Seoul, Republic of Korea

evidence.tested: Retrospective confirmatory assessment at the development center and external evaluation across 30,487 ICU admissions compared discrimination, lead time, calibration, and matched alarm burden.
evidence.unknown: No intervention effect is tested; performance does not establish clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: An existing recurrent-network and gradient-boosting ensemble estimates 12-hour cardiac-arrest risk from ICU data.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
